intro: Bangor is a city on the Penobscot River in Maine. On its northern edge the Bangor City Forest holds the Orono Bog Boardwalk, a walk out across a peat bog, and at the very start of that walk stands a huge twin-stemmed eastern white pine that a reader photographed and sent to us. We have no measurements for it yet, and we would like some.
meta_description: The big eastern white pine at the start of the Orono Bog Boardwalk in the Bangor City Forest, Maine: where it stands and what we know.
question_meta: The big eastern white pine at the start of the Orono Bog Boardwalk in the Bangor City Forest, Maine: where it stands and what we know.
question_answer: The White Pine at the Orono Bog Boardwalk stands beside the trailhead kiosk of the boardwalk in the Bangor City Forest, off Tripp Drive. It is free to see.
question_context: "It sits at the entrance of the Orono Bog Boardwalk, and is strikingly large," wrote the reader who sent us this eastern white pine from the Bangor City Forest in Maine, with a GPS fix taken beside it. The photograph shows exactly that. Every walker on the boardwalk passes it first. The roofed kiosk with the trail map stands at its left, the planks of the boardwalk set off into the bog on its right, and between them the pine rises far above the birches and spruces around it. A single ridged grey trunk, wide at the foot, splits a little way up into two tall stems that climb side by side into a crown of soft blue-green needles. Near the top of one stem a dead spike of bare silvered wood shows where a leader once broke. White pines are the tallest trees of eastern North America, and Maine is called the Pine Tree State after them. We have no girth, height or age for this one yet. If you have measured it, tell us here and we will add your figures. Stop at the kiosk before you step onto the boardwalk and look straight up.
